- When sentiment is negative (e.g., -0.25) in recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- Model consistently overestimates early in 30-day horizon, especially after recent price spikes; apply downward bias of 2–5% for first 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high.
- If sentiment is neutral or positive (0.00), model tends to overreact to short-term volatility; apply smoothing filter to reduce noise in 3–5 day window.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30-day forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 3–7% to align with historical mean reversion pattern.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate downward moves; if true outcome shows >3% drop from prior day, reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid “sell-off” overreaction.
